title: A substituted Cohen relation retains a nonzero parameter class
statement:
Let $V$ be a Cohen ring with uniformizer the prime integer $p$ [def-weil-pbc-cohen-ring] and residue field $k=V/pV$. Let $K$ be a finite free abelian group, $S,T$ sharp fine saturated additive monoids [def-trf-fs-log-blowup] (sharp: $0$ is the only invertible element), and $f:S\to K\oplus T$ a homomorphism with coordinates $(\delta,\beta)$ and $\beta(s)\ne0$ for $s\ne0$. Fix $n\ge0$ and put $t=(t_1,\ldots,t_n)$,
$$E=V[K][t],\quad\mathfrak p\subset E\text{ a prime containing }(p,t),\quad E_*=E_{\mathfrak p},\quad D=\widehat {E_*},$$
$$H_S=\widehat {V[S][t]}_{(p,[s]:s\ne0,t)},\quad H=D[[T]]=\widehat {D[T]}_{(\mathfrak m_D,[v]:v\ne0)}.$$
Completions and localization are [def-weil-pbc-adic-completion, def-weil-pbc-localization-at-prime], and Monoid rings $E[M]$ consist of finite sums $\sum c_u[u]$ with $[u][v]=[u+v]$. There is a continuous substitution homomorphism $\psi:H_S\to H$ extending $V\to D$, $t_i\mapsto t_i\in D$, $[s]\mapsto[\delta(s)][\beta(s)]$. For every $\theta\in H_S$ with $\theta-p\in([s]:s\ne0,t)H_S$, set $\eta=\psi(\theta)$ and let $\bar\eta\in D$ be its image under the augmentation $H\to D$ killing the nonzero $T$-monomials. Then
$$\bar\eta\equiv p\pmod{(t)D},\qquad\bar\eta\in\mathfrak m_D\setminus\mathfrak m_D^2.$$
More precisely, with $E'=E_* /(t)$ and maximal ideal $\mathfrak m_{E'}$, both $E'$ and $E'/pE'$ are regular local [def-weil-regular-scheme]; $p$ is nonzero and lies in $\mathfrak m_{E'}\setminus\mathfrak m_{E'}^2$, $D/(t)D\cong\widehat {E'}$, and the image of $\bar\eta$ in this quotient is $p$, whose cotangent class remains nonzero. This asserts congruence modulo the old parameters, allowing linear $t_i$ terms, including $\theta=p-t_1$.

proof.text: Choose a basis of $K$, of rank $r$. Thus $V[K]=V[z_1^{\pm1},\ldots,z_r^{\pm1}]$: the basis monomial indexed by $(a_i)$ is $\prod z_i^{a_i}$, and the inverse sends $z_i^{\pm1}$ to the corresponding group basis elements. A Cohen ring and a field are regular local rings, by [lem-weil-pbc-power-series-field-cohen-regular-complete] with zero variables. They are therefore regular rings by [lem-weil-pbc-regular-local-localization]. Apply [lem-trf-polynomial-ring-regular-base] over $V$ (including the old variables $t$) and over $k$, and then [lem-weil-pbc-localization-of-regular-ring] to invert the $z_i$ and localize at primes. Consequently $E_*$ is Noetherian regular local, as are every prime localization of $V[K]$ and of $k[K]$.

proof.text:
Put $\mathfrak q=\mathfrak p/(t)\subset V[K]$. The explicit isomorphism $E'=E_*/(t)\cong V[K]_{\mathfrak q}$ sends the class of $a(t)/b(t)$ to $a(0)/b(0)$: $b
otin\mathfrak p$ implies $b(0)
otin\mathfrak q$, and its inverse is induced by constant polynomials. Reducing coefficients modulo $p$ gives in the same way $E'/pE'\cong k[K]_{\mathfrak q/(p)}$. Both rings are regular local by Step 1. Moreover $p
e0$ in $E'$: if a denominator $b
otin\mathfrak q$ killed $p$ in $V[K]$, each coefficient of $b$ would be killed by the nonzero element $p$ of the domain $V$, hence $b=0$, impossible. Since $p\in\mathfrak q$, its image belongs to the maximal ideal $\mathfrak m'$ of $E'$.

proof.text: Apply [lem-weil-pbc-regular-local-quotient-independent-generators] to $R=E'$ and $I=pE'$. Its hypotheses hold by Steps 1--2. It gives a finite set generating $pE'$ whose cotangent classes in $\mathfrak m'/\mathfrak m'^2$ are linearly independent. If $p$ lay in $\mathfrak m'^2$, every element of this generating set would have zero cotangent class. Independence would force the set to be empty, hence $pE'=0$, contradicting $p\ne0$. Thus $p\in\mathfrak m'\setminus\mathfrak m'^2$.

proof.text: The surjection $E_*\to E'$ has kernel $(t)$ and $E_*$ is Noetherian local. Thus [lem-weil-pbc-local-completion-quotient] gives the canonical isomorphism $D/(t)D\cong\widehat {E'}$, carrying $p$ to $p$. By [lem-weil-pbc-local-completion-local-ring], $D$ and $\widehat {E'}$ are local, with maximal ideals obtained by extending those of $E_*$ and $E'$. By [lem-weil-pbc-module-completion-complete], applied with $M=E'$ and $I=\mathfrak m'$, $E'/\mathfrak m'^2\cong\widehat {E'}/\mathfrak m'^2\widehat {E'}$ through the canonical map. Therefore the image of $p$ in $\widehat {E'}$ is outside its maximal ideal squared, by Step 3. The same completion lemma for $E_*$ says $D$ is complete for its maximal ideal. All ideals here are finitely generated because the original local rings are Noetherian.

proof.text:
Let $I=(p,[s]:s
e0,t)\subset V[S][t]$ and $J=(\mathfrak m_D,[v]:v
e0)\subset D[T]$. The map on finite monoid sums sends $c[s]t^a$ to $c[\delta(s)][ eta(s)]t^a$; additivity of $f$ makes it multiplicative. Its image of $I$ is in $J$: $p,t_i\in\mathfrak m_D$ and $ eta(s)
e0$ for $s
e0$. For each $l\ge1$ it therefore induces $V[S][t]/I^l	o D[T]/J^l$. Apply these compatible maps to the coordinates of a compatible sequence to obtain $\psi:H_S	o H$. This is a ring homomorphism, extends the prescribed map, and is continuous since its $l$-th coordinate depends only on the $l$-th coordinate of the input. Sharpness of $T$ implies that two nonzero elements cannot sum to zero: otherwise each would be invertible. Hence killing nonzero $T$-monomials defines an augmentation $D[T]	o D$, carrying $J^l$ into $\mathfrak m_D^l$. Taking compatible coordinates and using completeness of $D$ from Step 4 gives the continuous augmentation $H	o D$; it fixes $D$ and kills every nonzero $T$-monomial.

proof.text:
Write $	heta-p=\sum_{j=1}^h[s_j]b_j+\sum_{i=1}^nt_i c_i$ with each $s_j
e0$; this is the definition of membership in the stated generated ideal. Apply the augmentation after $\psi$. Each first summand vanishes since $ eta(s_j)
e0$. Thus $ ar\eta=p+\sum_i t_i a_i$ for $a_i\in D$, proving the congruence and $ ar\eta\in\mathfrak m_D$. Its image in $D/(t)D\cong\widehat {E'}$ is exactly $p$. The quotient sends $\mathfrak m_D$ into the maximal ideal of $\widehat {E'}$: on $E_*$ this follows from the quotient $E_*	o E'$, and Step 4 identifies both completed maximal ideals with the extended ones. It therefore sends $\mathfrak m_D^2$ into that ideal squared. Step 4 shows $p$ is outside this square, so $ ar\eta
otin\mathfrak m_D^2$. The argument allows $n=0$, trivial $K,S,T$, and $	heta=p-t_1$ without change.
